subject: general
question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): The Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) is widely recognized as the workhorse launch vehicle of ISRO.

Reason (R): PSLV is highly versatile, capable of launching a diverse range of payloads into various Earth orbits (including Earth Observation, small Geosynchronous, and Navigation satellites), and boasts an exceptionally high mission success rate across its different variants.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A):** The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** is widely recognized as the workhorse launch vehicle of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). This statement is **true** as PSLV has been instrumental in launching numerous satellites for a variety of purposes since its inception.
 
• **Reason (R):** PSLV is highly versatile, capable of launching a diverse range of payloads into different Earth orbits, including **Earth Observation satellites**, **small Geosynchronous satellites**, and **Navigation satellites**. Additionally, PSLV boasts an exceptionally high mission success rate across its different variants. This statement is also **true**, and it explains why PSLV is regarded as ISRO’s workhorse.
 
• PSLV was first launched on **September 20, 1993**, and has since been used for **multiple missions**, including **interplanetary missions** such as the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan).
 
• The PSLV is known for its **reliability and flexibility**, having launched satellites into **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**, **Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit**, and **Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
• The statement "Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A" aptly explains the significance and versatility of PSLV in ISRO's space programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV):**

 
 
• The PSLV is a four-stage launch vehicle developed by ISRO, with alternate solid and liquid propulsion systems.
 
• It has launched satellites not only for India but also for **international customers**, making it a globally recognized launch vehicle.
 
• PSLV-C37 set a world record by successfully launching **104 satellites** in a single mission on **February 15, 2017**.
 
• The PSLV has variants such as PSLV-XL, PSLV-G, and PSLV-CA, each designed for specific payload capacities and mission requirements.
 
 
 
• **ISRO:**
 
 
• ISRO, established in **1969**, is India’s space agency responsible for space exploration and satellite development.
 
• It has developed multiple launch vehicles, including the **GSLV** (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) and **SSLV** (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle).
 
• ISRO’s achievements include missions like **Chandrayaan-1**, **Mangalyaan**, and **Chandrayaan-3**, demonstrating its technological prowess.
 
 
 
• **Satellite Launch Missions:**
 
 
• PSLV has launched satellites for applications like **remote sensing**, **navigation**, **communication**, and **climate monitoring**.
 
• Examples include the **Cartosat series** for Earth observation and **NavIC satellites** for navigation.
 
 
 
• **International Collaboration:**
 
 
• PSLV has launched satellites for countries like **USA**, **Germany**, **Canada**, and **Japan**, strengthening ISRO’s global footprint.
 
• This has contributed to ISRO’s reputation as a **cost-effective and reliable space agency**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **PSLV Variants:**

 
 
• **PSLV-XL:** Extended configuration used for heavier payloads.
 
• **PSLV-CA:** Core-alone version without strap-on boosters, suitable for smaller payloads.
 
• **PSLV-G:** Standard configuration designed for medium payloads.
 
 
 
• **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan):**
 
 
• Launched on **November 5, 2013**, using PSLV-C25.
 
• India became the **first nation** to reach Mars in its maiden attempt.
 
• The mission showcased PSLV’s capability to carry out **interplanetary missions**.
 
 
 
• **World Record:**
 
 
• PSLV’s ability to launch **104 satellites** in one mission highlights its efficiency and versatility.
